diagnostic_evidence.quote: n_t(x)\coloneqq x-\Pi_t(x)$ is in the normal space at $\Pi_t(x)$

issues.failure_explanation: The proof claims 2<n,Y_t> = 2||n||^2, but Y_t = z + n with z = Π(Y_t) a ridge point and n in the normal space at z. The normal-space condition implies n ⊥ T_z(ℝ_t), not n ⊥ z, so <n,z> is generally nonzero. The correct expansion is 2<n,Y_t> = 2||n||^2 + 2<n,z>.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the missing term 2<n,z> and bound it by 2ρ_{T-t}R, absorbing it into the existing additive error term 2ρ_{T-t}S_{T-t} (replacing S_{T-t} by S_{T-t}+R). This is a local change that preserves the theorem statement and all asymptotics.
issues.overall_effect: The derived drift bound for E[D] is missing the additive term 2<n,z>, which can be bounded by 2ρR and absorbed into existing error terms. The contraction rate and asymptotic scalings survive, but the proof as written is invalid.
issues.title: Dropped cross term 2<n,z> in normal-contraction drift
issues.why_classification: A short local addition of a bounded term to the error bound preserves every claim and guarantee; no new lemma or construction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the error $e_A(t,\cdot)=m(t,\cdot)-m_A(t,\cdot)$ within the normal space

issues.failure_explanation: With e_A = m − m_A (the appendix convention) the drift difference is b_A − b = −(2/h)e_A, so 2<n,b_A−b> = −(4/h)<n,e_A>. The proof writes +(2/h)<n,e_A> instead. The sign and the magnitude (factor 2) are both wrong. Young's inequality applied to the correct term (4/h)||n||||e_A^⊥|| yields an error coefficient 2/(βh²) rather than the 1/(βh²) used, and a contraction rate −(β−2) rather than −2(β−1).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the drift difference to −(4/h)<n,e_A> (with e_A = m − m_A) and re-apply Young's inequality with the resulting factor, giving contraction −(β−2) and error coefficient 2/(βh²). The stated O(·) bounds then follow with adjusted hidden constants.
issues.overall_effect: The derived differential inequality has the wrong error coefficient and a contraction rate approximately half of what is computed. Because the final theorem bound is stated in Θ/𝒪 notation with hidden constants and is loose enough to accommodate the weaker contraction, the theorem statement survives after a constant-factor adjustment.
issues.title: Wrong sign and factor of 2 on the e_A error term in normal-contraction drift
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local coefficient and sign fix in one inequality step; all asymptotic rates in the theorem statement survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the normal and tangential mean-errors scale like $\delta^c \int_\delta^{T-\tilde{t}_{in}} h_t^{1-c}/{w(t)} \dee t$ and $\delta^{1/2} \int_\delta^{T-\tilde{t}_{in}} h_t^{1/2}/{w(t)} \dee t$ respectively

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting w = 1 into the remark's own tangent formula gives δ^{1/2}∫h^{1/2}dt = O(δ^{1/2}), not O(δ²). Substituting w = h gives δ^{1/2}∫h^{−1/2}dt = O(δ^{1/2}), not O(δ). The normal formula gives O(δ^c) for both w = 1 and w = h (with c ∈ [1/2,1)), not O(δ²) or O(δ). Only the w = h² rate O(1) is correct. The claimed rate separation between w = 1 and w = h does not exist.

failure_location.quote: the mean-errors along both directions yield $\mc{O}(1),\mc{O}(\delta),\mc{O}(\delta^2)$ respectively

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute both integrals in the remark's own formulas: for w = 1 and w = h, both give tangent mean-error Θ(δ^{1/2}) and normal mean-error Θ(δ^c). State the corrected rates and note that w = 1 and w = h share the same δ-exponent, differing only in constants.
issues.overall_effect: The quantitative prediction that training weights w = 1 and w = h induce different δ-rate inductive biases is unsupported. Both yield the same asymptotic rate O(δ^{1/2}) (tangent) and O(δ^c) (normal); only w = h² is qualitatively different (O(1)). The experiments' qualitative ordering of error magnitudes is not contradicted.
issues.title: Incorrect δ-rates for w = 1 and w = h in training-weight remark
issues.why_classification: The repair is a contained recomputation of two integrals, but the claimed rate separation between w = 1 and w = h (δ² vs δ) is lost. The qualitative conclusion that w = h² gives O(1) errors survives; the recognisable framework is preserved but the quantitative prediction materially changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The main-text theorem states the tangent dimension-error as dδ but the formal appendix version gives dδ^{1/2}, and Theorem them:tangent contraciton itself bounds this term as O(d√δ) = O(dδ^{1/2}). Since δ < 1 implies dδ < dδ^{1/2}, the main-text statement claims a strictly stronger rate than what any proof in the paper establishes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change dδ to dδ^{1/2} in the tangent-error bound of Theorem thm:informal inference to training, matching the formal appendix statement and Theorem them:tangent contraciton. Propagate the corrected rate to the remainder of Theorem thm:directional decomposition.
issues.overall_effect: The tangent-error bound in Theorem thm:informal inference to training overstates the convergence rate of the dimension-error contribution. The bound with the correct rate dδ^{1/2} is stated in the appendix and follows from Theorem them:tangent contraciton. Theorem thm:directional decomposition references the informal theorem and inherits the too-optimistic rate in its remainder.
issues.title: Tangent dimension-error dδ overclaims relative to dδ^{1/2} in formal theorem
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single exponent correction in one displayed bound, matching the rate already proved in the appendix; all substantive claims and guarantees survive with the correct exponent.
